P1.evidence: Setter notes read back well — 'I went through what Kim spoke with you about. So, I have some information about you. You're 49, right?' — and he used them to confirm age, weight, body fat, sports and diet. But no four-part frame was set and no frame agreement was sought; the nearest thing was 'We'll get into every nitty-gritty detail, because I'm kind of an old-school guy.' The open question arrived late and in a different form at 00:07:46: 'help me understand, like, what's actually driving this for you right now?'

P2.evidence: Age, weight and body fat confirmed from setter notes but height never established. Work covered properly: 'in terms of work, like, what do you do? Are you mostly at desk or moving around?' Health asked but not hereditary: 'any health stuff I should know about? Anything beyond the shoulder and trap issues you mentioned?' Injuries probed twice, including duration and how often they sideline him. Training week covered for both jiu-jitsu and kettlebells, including the on/off pattern. Diet covered via the setter note on carnivore plus a junk-food question. Sleep was never asked — the prospect volunteered 'I also was struggling. I to sleep for the past couple months' at 00:43:38, forty-three minutes in. Energy never asked; 'had some fatigue' surfaced unprompted at 00:47:07.

P3.evidence: Opened goals with an outcome question rather than the scripted one-thing-you-would-change: 'if everything went perfectly over the next six months, like, what does that actually look like for you?' Never asked what he physically wants to do but cannot. The bridge and the moving-better question both landed cleanly: 'And outside of that physical side, what does that actually give you? Like when you're moving better... what does that change for you?' He never asked who else it impacts — the prospect volunteered his five- and eight-year-olds himself. The reflect-back was the strongest move on the call: 'It isn't really about getting more shredded, which is like a byproduct. This is about, like, being the guy who's still performing at elite level, keeping yourself to the high standard in his 50s, in his 60s even, for jiu-jitsu, for your kids especially' — answered 'Yeah.'

P4.evidence: Past attempts surfaced in detail — Onnit, Simple & Sinister, single-heavy-set work — via 'you've been training with kettlebells on and off for some years?' and 'How did it actually look like, especially the on and off part, like what happens, like, what does off like look for you when you don't do it?' Root cause asked directly: 'what do you think, like, what's actually been missing, like, what's the biggest missing piece over here for you?' The prospect named the gap himself — no structure, too many conflicting protocols, 'I don't know which one to do' and 'I'm coachable. I like to have a coach in every aspect of my life.' The rep then generalised it well to former athletes needing structure. The scripted 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' was never asked.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at all. No two-year question, no settle-for question, no line in the sand. The closest adjacent move was an injury-cost aside during the goals section — 'if you catch an injury, you're going to be off for one month, two months. That's even worse' — which the rep used to justify programme design, not to make the cost of inaction real. This is the heaviest miss on the call and it is why the timing objection later had nothing to push against.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran and landed: 'if you had this like right structure that we were talking about, and the right progression... Do you believe you could actually get there to be the fittest dad on earth?' Answer: 'Yeah, I mean, I would get it done. Totally.' But the all-in question was never asked, and the prospect immediately attached a condition — 'If I'm going to pay for a coach, the first step is to see, what is this? What does the accountability look like?' — which the rep treated as a green light and moved straight into the three-pillar presentation rather than returning to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. Price was disclosed on the prospect's request, the prospect gated on pending medical results, and the rep moved directly to scheduling a follow-up: 'How about tomorrow, the same time, like today?' ... '11 on Friday.' No payment ask, no Trevor onboarding call, no agreement email, no Skool or questionnaire instructions.

objection_plays.detail: No think-about-it objection. The hesitation was specific and medical, not deliberative.
Spouse never raised as a decision gate.

No money objection. The prospect pre-empted the price with a supportive anchor ($10,000 for three months of guitar lessons) and said 'I figured it'd be around that somewhere around that' when he heard $6,000. The rep nonetheless volunteered a payment-flexibility hint unprompted — 'That depends. Like most guys take it upfront. Um, maybe in your case, it's, it's not a necessity' — which is an OC move fired with no OC trigger present.

A genuine timing objection landed — 'I'm holding off on this until I get through these tests' and 'I want to make sure that I'm not putting money down until I get [results]'. No OD move ran: no things-never-slow-down, no when-does-it-become-the-right-time, no longer-you-wait. Declining to run the play was the right call here because the trigger was clinical rather than avoidant, but the rep also did not replace it with anything — he accommodated, explained the symptoms himself, and rebooked.
No fear-of-failure or doubt-about-the-method objection. The prospect was pre-sold on the modality.

Script gap. The prospect is mid-diagnostic-workup for possible gallstones with surgery on the table, on top of a history of herniated discs and recurrent thoracic inflammation. There is no scripted path for 'I have an undiagnosed active condition and I want clearance before I start.' The rep improvised toward keeping the deal alive — offering to enrol now, start mobility only, and pause if surgery happens — where the process needs an explicit clinical-clearance step that says the opposite. Same shape as the Tyron Giuliani gap already logged in the playbook, but here it arrives before diagnosis rather than after.

notes: Excellent rapport, strong root-cause work and the single best reflect-back in the phase set, undermined by skipping the consequence frame entirely and never asking the all-in question — so when the medical hold arrived there was no accumulated urgency and nothing to isolate against. Coach on P5 and P6b, on asking sleep and energy in baseline rather than letting them fall out at minute 43, and on adding a clinical-clearance step before any 'we can get you in' language when a prospect has diagnostics pending.
